Rashi on Kiddushin 65b:10:1.hebrew: או דלמא - שאפילו הם מודים, אין דבריהם קיימים אלא בעדים; ונמצא אני מחזיק בשלו והוא בשלי, שאין חלוקתנו כלום:
Rashi on Kiddushin 65b:10:1.english: Or perhaps - That even if they admit, their words are not established except through witnesses; and [consequently] it turns out that I am holding his [share] and he is holding mine, for our division is nothing.

Rashi on Kiddushin 65b:10:2.hebrew: לשקרי - הכופרים בדברים, לומר: "לא כן הוא":
Rashi on Kiddushin 65b:10:2.english: For liars - Those who deny the matters, saying: "It is not so."

Rashi on Kiddushin 65b:11:1.hebrew: אכלת חלב - בשוגג, וחייב אתה קרבן:
Rashi on Kiddushin 65b:11:1.english: You ate [forbidden] fat - [You ate it] unwittingly, and you are obligated [to bring] an offering.

Rashi on Kiddushin 65b:11:2.hebrew: נאמן - העד, וכשר הקרבן. ואין כאן משום "או הודע אליו חטאתו" (ויקרא ד) — "ולא שיודיעוהו אחרים"; והכי דרשינן לה בשמעתא קמייתא דהאשה רבה (ד' פז:): "ולא שיודיעוהו אחרים" — והוא מכחיש:
Rashi on Kiddushin 65b:11:2.english: [Is] deemed credible - The witness [is believed], and the [sin-]offering is valid. And there is no [concern] here on account of "or [if] his sin be made known to him" (Leviticus 4) — "and not that others make it known to him"; for this is how we interpret it in the first sugya of [the chapter entitled] HaIsha Rabbah (87b): "And not that others make it known to him" — [applies only] when he denies [it].

Rashi on Kiddushin 65b:1:1.hebrew: אמרינן הן הן עדי יחוד כו' - משראוה שנתייחדה עמו, אין צריך להעיד על הביאה, דכיון דלבו גס בה, מחזקינן אותו בחזקת שבא עליה לשם קידושין:
Rashi on Kiddushin 65b:1:1.english: We say: These are the witnesses of seclusion, etc. - Once they saw that she was secluded with him, there is no need to testify about the act of intercourse, for since he is accustomed to her, we maintain him under the presumption that he engaged in intercourse with her for the sake of betrothal.

Rashi on Kiddushin 65b:2:1.hebrew: ואיכא דאמרי - דרבה משמיה דרב אמר, ומאן קרי רב בי דינא רבה? רבי:
Rashi on Kiddushin 65b:2:1.english: And there are those who say - That Rabba said [this] in the name of Rav; and whom does Rav call "the Great Court"? Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi].

Rashi on Kiddushin 65b:3:1.hebrew: צריכה שני גיטין - קס"ד, כדי להתירה לינשא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 65b:3:1.english: She requires two bills of divorce - It enters [one's] mind [that this is] in order to permit her to marry.

Rashi on Kiddushin 65b:3:2.hebrew: וגובה כתובתה מן החבילה - ממה נפשך, והמותר מוטל בספק עד יבא אליהו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 65b:3:2.english: And she collects her marriage contract from the bundle - Whichever way you look at it; and the remainder is left in doubt until Elijah comes.

Rashi on Kiddushin 65b:4:1.hebrew: אי דאית ליה סהדי להאי - שאמר: ״בפנינו קדשה״, ואית ליה סהדי נמי להאי:
Rashi on Kiddushin 65b:4:1.english: If this one has witnesses - who said: "In our presence he betrothed her," and that one also has witnesses [testifying likewise].

Rashi on Kiddushin 65b:4:2.english: Can she say, etc. - That the remainder of the marriage contract should be hers and theirs in doubt.

Rashi on Kiddushin 65b:4:3.hebrew: אלא לאו בעד אחד - לכל אחד, וש"מ דאפי' אינה מודה — צריכה גט:
Rashi on Kiddushin 65b:4:3.english: Rather, is it not with one witness - [That is, one witness] for each one; and learn from this that even if she does not admit [it], she requires a bill of divorce.

Rashi on Kiddushin 65b:5:1.hebrew: עד אחד בהכחשה - דאיכא חד סהדא דמכחיש ליה, מי מהימן? אפי' לא מכחשא ליה איהי — ליכא למאן דאמר, דאין האחד בא אלא לשבועה, והכא שבועה לא שייכא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 65b:5:1.english: A single witness in [the face of] contradiction - Where there is one witness who contradicts him, is he believed? Even if she does not contradict him, there is no authority who says [that he is believed], for a single [witness] comes only to [obligate] an oath, and here an oath is not applicable.

Rashi on Kiddushin 65b:6:1.hebrew: צריכה שני גיטין - כדי לגבות כתובתה מן החבילה. כלומר: לעולם החבילה מונחת עד שיבא אליהו, אלא א"כ נתנו לה שניהם גט מעצמן, והגט מביאה לידי גיבוי כתובה מן החבילה ממה נפשך: אם של זה הוא — הרי מיחייב לה כתובה על פיו, וכן זה; וכ"ש אם כולה שלה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 65b:6:1.english: She requires two bills of divorce - [This is] in order to collect her marriage contract from the bundle. That is to say: [Ordinarily,] the bundle would remain deposited until Elijah comes, unless both of them gave her a bill of divorce of their own accord; and the bill of divorce brings her to the collection of [her] marriage contract from the bundle, whichever way you look at it: if it belongs to this one, he is obligated [to pay] her a marriage contract according to his own admission, and likewise this [other one]; and all the more so if it is entirely hers.

Rashi on Kiddushin 65b:6:2.hebrew: ור"מ היא וכו' - כלומר, וכולה לא אשמועינן אלא דמטלטלין משתעבדי לכתובה. ור"מ היא, דאמר במס' כתובות, בהאשה שנפלו לה נכסים (דף פ:), גבי שומרת יבם שכתובתה על נכסי בעלה הראשון: הניח אחיו מעות — ילקח בהם קרקע והוא אוכל פירות; אלמא, מעות משתעבדי לכתובה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 65b:6:2.english: And it is Rabbi Meir, etc. - That is to say, the entire [baraita] only comes to teach us that movable property is subject to a lien for a marriage contract. And it is [in accordance with] Rabbi Meir, who said in Tractate Ketubot, in [the chapter] "HaIsha SheNafelu Lah Nekhasim" (page 80b), regarding a woman awaiting levirate marriage whose marriage contract is [payable] from the estate of her first husband: [If] his brother left money, land shall be purchased with it, and he consumes the produce — thus, money is subject to a lien for a marriage contract.

Rashi on Kiddushin 65b:8:1.hebrew: הודאת בעל דין כמאה עדים - דכתיב (שמות כב): "אשר יאמר כי הוא זה" — הרי שסמך הכתוב על מקצת הודאתו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 65b:8:1.english: The admission of a litigant is like one hundred witnesses - As it is written (Exodus 22:8): "About which one says: This is it" — behold, [Scripture] relied upon his partial admission.

Rashi on Kiddushin 65b:8:2.hebrew: לא קא חייב לאחריני - אינו חב לאחרים בהודאתו זו, שאין נפסד אלא הוא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 65b:8:2.english: He does not cause detriment to others - He does not cause disadvantage to others with this admission of his, for no one suffers a loss except him.

Rashi on Kiddushin 65b:8:3.hebrew: הכא קא חייבה לאחריני - שקרובותיה נאסרו בו, וקרוביו נאסרין בה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 65b:8:3.english: Here he causes liability to others - For her relatives become forbidden to him, and his male relatives become forbidden to her.

Rashi on Kiddushin 65b:9:1.hebrew: בני רב מרי - גרס, אחים הוו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 65b:9:1.english: The sons of Rav Mari - Is the reading, [for] they were brothers.

Rashi on Kiddushin 65b:9:2.hebrew: על פי שנים - שהצריכה תורה, למאי הלכתא הצריך עדים? משום דאי בעי למיהדר ולומר "לא כך היה", לא יוכל לומר כן, שאלו יעידום — הוא שהצריכם הכתוב עדים; ואנו, אין אנו שקרנים, ולא הדרינן בן, ואין אנו צריכין עדים:
Rashi on Kiddushin 65b:9:2.english: At the mouths of two [witnesses] - [In] that the Torah required [them] — for what legal purpose did it require witnesses? [Is it] because if [one] wishes to retract and say, “It was not so,” he will not be able to say so, for these [witnesses] will testify against them — [and that] is why Scripture required witnesses for them? And [as for] us, we are not liars and we will not retract, and [therefore] we do not need witnesses.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 65b:10:1.hebrew: לא איברו סהדי אלא לשקרי - מכאן אמר ר"ת דאין צריך עדים לעשות קנין. והא דאמר פרק חזקת הבתים (ב"ב דף מ.): "קנין בפני שנים, ואין צריך לומר כתובו" — לאו משום דלא מהני בלא שנים, דודאי מהני אפי' בלא שנים; אלא ה"ק: קנין הרגיל בפני שנים — אין צריך לומר כתובו, אבל ודאי אין צריך שנים. וכן משמע בפרק הזהב (ב"מ דף מה:), דקאמר התם: "היה עומד בגורן ואין בידו מעות" כו', ופריך עלה: "וניקנינהו ניהליה אגב סודר", ומשני: "דלית ליה סודר". ואמאי לא משני דלא היו שם עדים? אלא ש"מ דקנין מהני בלא עדים. וכן משמע בפ"ק דסנהדרין (דף ו.), דקאמר התם: "פשרה ביחיד", וקי"ל (שם) דפשרה צריכה קנין:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 65b:10:1.english: Witnesses were created only for liars - From here Rabbeinu Tam stated that witnesses are not required in order to effect a transaction [kinyan]. And that which [the Gemara] says in the chapter [entitled] Chezkas HaBattim (Bava Batra 40a): "[A transaction executed through a] kinyan [is performed] before two [witnesses], and [the buyer] does not need to say [to them], 'Write [a deed], '" [this is] not because it is ineffective without two [witnesses], for it is certainly effective even without two; rather, this is what it means: [For] a kinyan, which is customarily [performed] before two [witnesses], one does not need to say, "Write [a deed]"; but certainly, two [witnesses] are not required [for the kinyan to take effect]. And so it is implied in the chapter [entitled] HaZahav (Bava Metzia 45b), where it says there: "[If one] was standing in the threshing floor and did not have money in his hand, etc.," and it objects to this: "Then let him acquire them for him by means of a cloth [kinyan sudar]!", and answers: "Where he did not have a cloth." But why does it not answer that there were no witnesses present there? Rather, conclude from this that a kinyan is effective without witnesses. And so it is implied in the first chapter of Sanhedrin (6a), where it says there: "Mediation [may be conducted] by a single [individual]," and we maintain (there) that mediation requires a kinyan.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 65b:11:1.hebrew: אמר לו עד אחד אכלת חלב והלה שותק נאמן - פירוש: דשתיקה כהודאה דמי, והוי נודע לו מעצמו. אבל אמר לו "איני יודע" — אינו נאמן לחייבו קרבן, דכתיב (ויקרא ד׳:כ״ג): "או הודע אליו" — ולא שיודיעוהו אחרים. ודווקא אחד; אבל שנים נאמנים, ומביא קרבן על ידם, כדאמר התם (כריתות דף יא:): "אם הביאוהו שנים לידי מיתה חמורה, לא יביאוהו לידי קרבן הקל?!" וצריך נמי לפרש: "והלה שותק" — דאמר לו העד: "אכלת חלב, והיה לך לידע", והוא שותק:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 65b:11:1.english: [If] one witness says to him: "You ate [forbidden] fat," and that one remains silent, [the witness is] believed - Explanation: For silence is equivalent to an admission, and [thus] it is considered [as if] it became known to him on his own. But if he said to him: "I do not know," [the witness] is not believed to obligate him in an offering, for it is written: "Or if [his sin] become known to him" (Leviticus 4:23) — and not that others make it known to him. And [this rule] applies specifically to one [witness]; but two [witnesses] are believed, and he brings an offering on their authority, as [the Gemara] says there (Keritot 11b): "If two [witnesses] can bring him to the severe [punishment of] death, shall they not bring him to the lenient [obligation of] an offering?!" And it is also necessary to explain [the phrase] "and that one remains silent" — that the witness said to him: "You ate [forbidden] fat, and you ought to know," and he remains silent.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 65b:11:2.hebrew: ותנא תונא והלה אומר לא אכלתי - הא דנקט "לא אכלתי", ה"ה אם אמר "איני יודע" דפטור, משום דכתיב (שם) "או הודע". והא דנקט "לא אכלתי" — משום דבעי למיתני סיפא גבי "שנים אומרים אכלת חלב והוא אומר לא אכלתי"; ובהא איכא רבותא לר"מ, דאפילו אמר "לא אכלתי" מחייב ר"מ:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 65b:11:2.english: "And the tanna also taught: 'And that [person] says: I did not eat'" - The fact that [the mishna] formulated [it as] "I did not eat," the same law applies if he said "I do not know," that he is exempt, because it is written: "Or if [his sin] be made known to him" (ibid., Leviticus 4:23). And the fact that [the mishna] formulated [it as] "I did not eat" is because it needed to teach the closing clause regarding [a case where] "Two [witnesses] say: 'You ate forbidden fat,' and he says: 'I did not eat'"; and in this [case], there is a novelty according to Rabbi Meir, that even [if] he said "I did not eat," Rabbi Meir holds [him] liable.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 65b:12:1.hebrew: נטמאו טהרותיך והלה שותק נאמן - שאמר לו העד: "בפניך נטמאו". וכן צריך לפרש ב"אכלת חלב", כדפרישית. וקשה, דהא בפ' הנזקין (גיטין דף נד:) מייתי: "היה עושה עמו בטהרות ואמר לו ׳נטמאו טהרותיך׳ — נאמן; ׳טהרות שעשיתי עמך ביום פלוני נטמאו׳ — אינו נאמן". ופריך התם: מאי שנא רישא ומאי שנא סיפא? ומשני: אמר אביי, "כל שבידו — נאמן, וכל שאינו בידו — אינו נאמן; וסיפא איירי שאין הטהרות בידו, לכך אינו נאמן". והיכי אמר אביי דנאמן כשאמר לו "אכלת חלב", ואע"ג שאין בידו להאכילו חלב?! וכן קשה לקמן, דנאמן לומר "שורך נרבע", אע"ג דאין בידו להרביע שורו! וי"ל, דההיא דהנזקין מיירי כשאינו שותק, אלא מכחישו; והכא איירי כששותק, ואינו מכחישו. ומיהו קשה מרבא, דהכא משמע דלא פליג רבא עליה דאביי, דאמר דכל דבר שאין בידו בעי שותק; והתם קאמר רבא: "אשכחיה ולא אמר ליה, והדר אשכחיה ואמר ליה — אינו נאמן", משמע: אבל אי אמר ליה מיד — נאמן בכל ענין, אפי' אין בידו ואפי' אין שותק, והכא לא פליג אאביי דבאין בידו בעי שותק! וי"ל: שאני התם, לפי שהיה בידו פעם אחת, דהיינו בשעת שעשאו; אבל הכא, מעולם לא היה בידו כלל, ולכן בעי שותק. ונראה דהלכה כרבא לגבי אביי. ועתה בענין זה יש שלשה דינים: בדבר שהיה בידו, כגון ההיא ד"היה עושה עמו בטהרות" — נאמן, ואפי' לא היה שותק; ובדבר שאין בידו לעולם, כגון "אכלת חלב" ו"שורך נרבע" — אי שתיק מהימן, ואי לא שתיק לא מהימן; ובדבר שאין בידו עתה אבל היה בידו פעם אחרת — בהא פליגי אביי ורבא, כדפירשתי התם גבי "טהרות שעשיתי עמך", דלרבא היכא דאשכחיה ואמר ליה מהימן, ואפילו אינו שותק; והלכה כרבא כדפרישית. ושותק דאמר בשמעתין דנאמן, נראה לר"י דהיינו בדבר שיש לו לידע, כגון שאמר לו: "נתנסך יינך בפניך", דומיא ד"אכלת חלב"; אבל אם אמר לו: "נתנסך יינך שלא בפניך" ושותק — ההיא שתיקה אינה כהודאה, שלכך לא ישיב לו, לפי שלא היה יודע בירור הדבר. ומה שאמרנו דבר שאינו בידו כי אינו שותק לא מהימן — היינו גברא דלא מהימן כבי תרי; אבל אי מהימן ליה כבי תרי — נאמן, כדאמר בסמוך גבי סמיא, דקאמר רבא דנאמן, אע"ג דהוי דבר שבערוה ואין דבר שבערוה פחות משנים, כל שכן דנאמן במילתא אחריתי. וצריך לומר דהא דאמר בכל דוכתין (גיטין דף ב:) "עד אחד נאמן באיסורין" — היינו דוקא להתיר, כגון "בשר זו מנוקרת" או "חתיכה זו של שומן", אבל לאסור הדבר אינו נאמן, אלא כמו שפירשתי. והא דאמרינן דבדבר שאינו בידו כי אינו שותק לא מהימן — היינו דוקא בדבר שאינו יכול להתברר; אבל בדבר שיכול להתברר, כגון שאמר לו: "יש שרץ בטהרותיך" או "עובד כוכבים מנסך יינך, בא ואראך האיסור" — בהא ודאי יש לחוש לדבריו ולבדוק, כדאמר לקמן (עמוד ב) גבי בעל מום, דמצי אמר ליה "שלח ואחוי". וכשאדם עושה חבירו שליח לשמור יינו או להביא מן המרתף — נאמן, דהיינו בידו, ומהימן עליה כבי תרי כשסומך עליו; והא דבעינן שותק — היינו דוקא דלא עשאו שליח:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 65b:12:1.english: "Your ritually pure items were defiled," and that one is silent, he is believed - Meaning that the witness said to him: "They were defiled in your presence." And one must likewise explain [the earlier case of] "You ate forbidden fat," as I have explained. And this is difficult: for in the chapter [entitled] HaNizakin (Gittin 54b), [the Gemara] cites: "If one was preparing ritually pure items with him and said to him: 'Your ritually pure items were defiled,' he is believed; [if he said:] 'The ritually pure items that I prepared with you on such-and-such a day were defiled,' he is not believed." And [the Gemara] challenges there: What is the difference between the first clause and the latter clause? And it answers: Abaye said, "Whoever has the matter in his power is believed, and whoever does not have the matter in his power is not believed; and the latter clause deals with [a case where] the ritually pure items are no longer in his power, which is why he is not believed." And how could Abaye say [here] that he is believed when he said to him: "You ate forbidden fat," even though it is not in his power to feed him forbidden fat?! And so too it is difficult regarding what is stated later (66a), that [a single witness] is believed to say: "Your ox was used for bestiality," even though it is not in his power to have his ox used for bestiality! And one can say that that [baraita cited in] HaNizakin deals with [a case where] he is not silent, but rather contradicts him; whereas here it deals with [a case where] he is silent and does not contradict him. However, there is a difficulty from Rava: for here it implies that Rava does not disagree with Abaye, who says that for anything that is not in his power, he requires [the owner to be] silent; yet there [in Gittin 54b] Rava says: "If he met him and did not tell him, and then met him again and told him, he is not believed" — which implies: but if he told him immediately, he is believed in any case, even if it is not in his power and even if he is not silent! Yet here he does not disagree with Abaye that when it is not in his power, he requires [the owner to be] silent! And one can say: It is different there, because it was in his power once, namely at the time that he prepared them; but here, it was never in his power at all, and therefore it requires [him to be] silent. And it appears that the halakhah follows Rava against Abaye. And now, in this matter, there are three rules: In a matter that was in his power, such as that [case] where he was preparing ritually pure items with him, he is believed, even if [the owner] was not silent; and in a matter that is never in his power, such as "You ate forbidden fat" and "Your ox was used for bestiality," if he is silent he is believed, and if he is not silent he is not believed; and in a matter that is not in his power now, but was in his power at another time — regarding this Abaye and Rava disagree, as I explained there concerning "the ritually pure items that I prepared with you," for according to Rava, where he met him and told him [immediately] he is believed, and even if he is not silent; and the halakhah follows Rava, as I have explained. And as for the silent one regarding whom it is said in our sugya that [the witness] is believed — it appears to the Ri that this is specifically in a matter that he ought to know, such as where he said to him: "Your wine was poured as a libation in your presence," similar to "You ate forbidden fat"; but if he said to him: "Your wine was poured as a libation not in your presence" and he is silent, that silence is not [considered] like an admission, for that is why he does not answer him, because he did not know the facts of the matter clearly. And that which we said, that in a matter that is not in his power, when he is not silent, he is not believed — this applies [only to an ordinary] person who is not believed like two [witnesses]; but if he is believed by him like two [witnesses], he is believed, as [the Gemara] says nearby regarding the blind man (66a), where Rava says that he is believed even though it is a matter of forbidden sexual relations, and no matter of forbidden sexual relations [can be established by] fewer than two [witnesses] — all the more so that he is believed in any other matter! And one must say that that which [the Gemara] states everywhere (Gittin 2b) that "one witness is believed in [matters of ritual] prohibitions" — that is specifically to permit [an item], such as [attesting that] "this meat is porged" or "this piece is [permitted] fat"; but to forbid the item he is not believed, except as I have explained. And that which we said, that in a matter that is not in his power, when he is not silent, he is not believed — that is specifically in a matter that cannot be verified; but in a matter that can be verified, such as where he said to him: "There is a creeping animal in your ritually pure items," or "An idolater is pouring your wine as a libation, come and I will show you the forbidden act" — in this [case] one certainly must suspect his words and investigate, as [the Gemara] says later (66b) regarding a blemished [priest], where he can say to him: "Strip and show [me]." And when a person appoints his fellow as an agent to guard his wine or to bring [it] from the cellar, he is believed, for that is in his power and he is believed by him like two [witnesses] when he relies upon him. And that which we require [the owner to be] silent — that is specifically where he did not appoint him an agent.
